newsitem.title: MOZAMBIQUE: Investment in Mozambique increases nearly 25 pct.
newsitem.headline: Investment in Mozambique increases nearly 25 pct.

text.p: Direct foreign investment in Mozambique authorised in 1996 amounted to $445.5 million, according to the director of the Investment Promotion Centre (CPI).
In an interview published in the Saturday issue of the Maputo daily Noticias, Director Fernando Sumbana said this was an increase of 24.7 per cent on the 1995 figure.
The major investors are Portuguese (total value, $75 million), South Africans ($74 million) and British ($38 million).
Sumbana expected an enormous leap in foreign investment in 1997.

He thought the total for this year could be about $2 billion, largely because of South African plans to build an aluminium smelter using cheap hydro-electric power from a new dam on the Zambezi River in central Mozambique.
